title: Tire blowout while driving
text:
1. Grip the wheel firmly with both hands and keep steering straight — do NOT swerve suddenly.
2. Do NOT slam the brakes. Ease your foot off the gas and let the car slow on its own.
3. Turn on hazard lights and brake gently only once speed is low. Guide the car to the far shoulder or emergency bay.
4. Stop fully off the road, engage the handbrake, and place the early-warning device (triangle) behind the car.
5. Change to the spare only on flat, stable ground — otherwise call for roadside help and wait inside with seatbelts on.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Pumutok na gulong habang nagmamaneho
text:
1. Mahigpit na hawakan ang manibela ng dalawang kamay at panatilihing diretso — HUWAG biglang lumiko.
2. HUWAG biglang magpreno. Dahan-dahang alisin ang paa sa gas at hayaang bumagal nang kusa ang sasakyan.
3. Buksan ang hazard lights at bahagyang magpreno lang kapag mabagal na. Itabi sa malayong shoulder o emergency bay.
4. Humingintong tuluyan sa labas ng kalsada, i-handbrake, at ilagay ang early-warning device (triangle) sa likod ng sasakyan.
5. Magpalit ng reserba lang sa patag at matatag na lupa — kung hindi, tumawag ng roadside help at maghintay sa loob nang nakaseatbelt.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Brake failure (nawalan ng preno)
text:
1. Stay calm and pump the brake pedal fast and hard — pressure can build back in the lines.
2. Shift to a lower gear at once (engine braking slows the car). For automatics, shift to L or 2.
3. Pull the handbrake GRADUALLY — never yank it, or the car will spin. Hold the button to control it.
4. Turn on hazards and horn, steer toward uphill slopes, emergency escape ramps, or soft shoulders — never oncoming traffic.
5. As a last resort, scrape the side of the car along a guardrail to bleed speed. Get the brakes repaired before driving again.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Nawalan ng preno
text:
1. Huminahon at bombahin nang mabilis at mariin ang preno — puwedeng bumalik ang pressure sa linya.
2. Mag-shift agad sa mababang gear (engine braking ang magpapabagal). Sa automatic, ilipat sa L o 2.
3. Hilahin nang DAHAN-DAHAN ang handbrake — huwag biglain, iikot ang sasakyan. Hawakan ang button para makontrol.
4. Buksan ang hazard at busina, itungo sa paakyat, emergency escape ramp, o malambot na shoulder — huwag sa kasalubong.
5. Bilang huling paraan, ikaskas ang gilid ng sasakyan sa guardrail para bumagal. Ipaayos muna ang preno bago magmaneho ulit.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Engine overheating (nag-overheat)
text:
1. At the first warning (gauge in red, steam, or smell), turn OFF the aircon and turn the cabin HEATER on full — it pulls heat away from the engine.
2. Pull over safely at once and turn the engine OFF. Do NOT keep driving to 'reach a shop'.
3. NEVER open the radiator cap while hot — scalding coolant erupts. Wait at least 30 minutes until cool to the touch.
4. Check coolant and oil levels only when cool. Top up with water or coolant if available and look for burst hoses or leaks.
5. If steam turns to smoke or flames appear, leave the car, move away, and call the fire station. Otherwise call a mechanic or towing.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Nag-overheat ang makina
text:
1. Sa unang babala (gauge nasa pula, usok, o amoy), patayin ang aircon at buksan nang todo ang HEATER sa loob — hinihila nito ang init palayo sa makina.
2. Tumabi agad nang ligtas at patayin ang makina. HUWAG ipilit magmaneho para 'makarating sa talyer'.
3. HUWAG kailanman buksan ang radiator cap habang mainit — sasabog ang kumukulong coolant. Maghintay ng hindi bababa sa 30 minuto hanggang lumamig.
4. Tingnan lang ang coolant at langis kapag malamig na. Dagdagan ng tubig o coolant kung mayroon at hanapin ang pumutok na hose o tagas.
5. Kung naging apoy ang usok, lumayo sa kotse at tumawag sa bombero. Kung hindi, tumawag ng mekaniko o towing.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Dead battery — safe jumpstart
text:
1. Check first: cracked, leaking, or swollen battery means do NOT jumpstart — call for replacement instead. No smoking or flames nearby.
2. Connect in order: RED clamp to the DEAD battery positive (+), other RED end to the GOOD battery positive (+).
3. Then BLACK clamp to the GOOD battery negative (−), and the other BLACK end to unpainted metal on the dead car's engine — never to its negative terminal.
4. Start the good car, wait 2 minutes, then start the dead car. Remove cables in exact reverse order.
5. Drive at least 20 minutes to recharge, then have the battery and charging system tested — a battery that dies again needs replacement.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / Car Maker Safety Guidance

title: Lobat na baterya — ligtas na jumpstart
text:
1. Tingnan muna: kung bitak, tumatagas, o namamaga ang baterya, HUWAG mag-jumpstart — tumawag na lang para palitan. Bawal manigarilyo o mag-apoy sa paligid.
2. Ikabit nang sunud-sunod: PULANG clamp sa positive (+) ng LOBAT na baterya, ang kabilang PULA sa positive (+) ng MAAYOS na baterya.
3. Saka ITIM na clamp sa negative (−) ng maayos na baterya, at ang kabilang ITIM sa walang pinturang metal ng makina ng lobat — huwag sa negative terminal nito.
4. Paandarin ang maayos na kotse, maghintay ng 2 minuto, saka paandarin ang lobat. Alisin ang mga kable nang pabaligtad na pagkakasunod.
5. Magmaneho nang hindi bababa sa 20 minuto para mag-charge, saka ipatest ang baterya at charging system — ang bateryang nalobat ulit ay kailangang palitan.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / Car Maker Safety Guidance

title: Car stalled in flood water
text:
1. NEVER drive through flood water — even shallow water stalls engines and floats cars. Turn around, do not drown.
2. If the engine dies in flood: do NOT restart it — water inside the engine destroys it (hydrolock). Turn on hazards.
3. If water is still low and stable, shift to neutral and push the car to higher ground with help.
4. If water is rising: abandon the car immediately and move to high ground (see flood_entering_home). Never stay inside a sinking car.
5. Call towing only after water recedes. Do NOT start the engine until a mechanic clears it.
source: NDRRMC Flood Safety / LTO Driver's Manual

title: Tumirik ang kotse sa baha
text:
1. HUWAG kailanman magmaneho sa baha — kahit mababaw ay tumitirik ang makina at lumulutang ang kotse. Bumalik, huwag magpakalunod.
2. Kung namatay ang makina sa baha: HUWAG subukang paandarin ulit — sinisira ng tubig sa loob ang makina. Buksan ang hazard.
3. Kung mababaw pa at hindi tumataas ang tubig, ilagay sa neutral at itulak sa mataas na lugar kasama ng tutulong.
4. Kung tumataas ang tubig: iwanan agad ang kotse at pumunta sa mataas (tingnan ang flood_entering_home). Huwag manatili sa lumulubog na kotse.
5. Tumawag ng towing kapag humupa na ang tubig. HUWAG paandarin hangga't hindi sinasabi ng mekaniko.
source: NDRRMC Flood Safety / LTO Driver's Manual

title: Breakdown on the road (especially at night)
text:
1. Pull fully off the road onto the shoulder or emergency bay. Turn on hazards at once.
2. Place the early-warning device (triangle) well behind the car so other drivers see you early — farther at night and on curves.
3. On fast highways, stay INSIDE with seatbelts on. On slow roads, exit away from traffic and stand behind a barrier.
4. Call trusted help, roadside assistance, or the expressway patrol with your exact location and direction.
5. Keep doors locked while waiting. Accept help only from uniformed patrol or people you called — stay on the phone with family until help arrives.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety

title: Nasiraan sa daan (lalo na sa gabi)
text:
1. Itabi nang tuluyan sa shoulder o emergency bay. Buksan agad ang hazard.
2. Ilagay ang early-warning device (triangle) nang malayo sa likod para maagang makita ng ibang driver — mas malayo sa gabi at sa kurbada.
3. Sa mabilis na highway, MANATILI sa loob nang nakaseatbelt. Sa mabagal na kalsada, lumabas palayo sa trapiko at tumayo sa likod ng barrier.
4. Tumawag sa pinagkakatiwalaan, roadside assistance, o expressway patrol dala ang eksaktong lokasyon at direksyon.
5. Panatilihing nakalock ang pinto habang naghihintay. Tanggapin lang ang tulong mula sa naka-unipormeng patrol o tinawagan mo — manatili sa telepono sa pamilya hanggang dumating ang tulong.
source: LTO Driver's Manual / MMDA Road Safety
